Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Time for the main feature: the live game.

A quiz can be played many times (for example, a rehearsal and the real talk). Each time is a new game with its own players and answers. Games skip inactive questions.

The moderator's side:

- The quiz page gets the "Start a game" button. It creates a new game and opens its big-screen page for the moderator (it stays in the moderator area).
- Before the start, the big screen shows the quiz title, the join link as plain text, a QR code with the same link, and the number of players currently waiting for the quiz to start as "Players: 2". The join link is a full URL; the scheme can be left out (for example, `localhost:3000/play/K7RZX`).
- The "Start" button shows the first active question: the progress ("Question 1 of 3"), the question text, and the options. While the question is open, the big screen counts the players who answered as "Answers: 1 / 2" (players who answered / players currently in the game). The second counter is important for moderators 'cause it shows if they need to wait for more answers or not, are there any active players in the game.
- The "Finish" button closes the question. The big screen then shows the number of answers for each option and marks the correct options with "Correct".
- The "Next" button shows the next active question. On the last question, the button is "End quiz" instead, and it ends the game.
- After the end, the big screen shows "The quiz is over".

The player's side:

- A player opens the join link on a phone. No account is needed: the page asks for "Your name" and has the "Join" button. After joining, the player sees "Hi, <name>!" (for example, "Hi, Alice!") and waits for the start.
- The browser remembers the player: opening the join link again in the same browser continues the game as the same player.
- Players can join at any time before the end. After the end, the join link shows "The quiz is over" and does not let anyone join.
- During a question, the player sees the question text and its options as buttons. Tapping an option submits it at once, and the option is marked "Your answer". The player can change the answer until the question is closed; the last pick counts. Players must not be able to find out the correct answer, not even in the page source, before the question is closed.
- After "Finish", the player sees "Correct!", "Wrong!", or "No answer".
- After the end, the player sees "The quiz is over".

Everything is live: the big screen, the counters, and the phones follow the game without page reloads. Participants typically use crowded conference Wi-Fi.

  def save_with_option_rows(body:, active:, option_rows:)
    trimmed_body = body.to_s.strip
    non_empty_rows = option_rows.reject { |row| row[:body].to_s.strip.blank? }

    form_errors = []
    form_errors << "Question can't be blank" if trimmed_body.blank?
    form_errors << "Add at least two options" if non_empty_rows.size < 2
    if non_empty_rows.any? && non_empty_rows.none? { |row| row[:correct] }
      form_errors << "Mark at least one option as correct"
    end

    return form_errors if form_errors.any?

    transaction do
      self.body = trimmed_body
      self.active = active
      self.position ||= (quiz.questions.maximum(:position) || 0) + 1
      save!

      options.destroy_all
      non_empty_rows.each_with_index do |row, index|
        options.create!(
          body: row[:body].to_s.strip,
          correct: row[:correct],
          position: index + 1
        )
      end
    end

    []
  end
end

Crucially, I'm defining a `start_game!` method.  This method's responsibilities: retrieve active questions, raise an exception if there are no active questions, handle the whole process transactionally to ensure data integrity, create a new game instance with a unique code and an initial status of "lobby," and then iterate through the active questions to create game questions and associated game options within that game. Each question will be associated with game options which include correct answers.

Next, I'm focusing on the `Game` model, which I need to think through carefully.  I'm outlining the different states the game can be in using the `STATUSES` constant – "lobby", "question_open", "question_closed", and "finished". I'm implementing standard validations for presence and uniqueness of the game code, and also validating the status against the defined states.  I'm also including helper methods for each status check (`lobby?`, `question_open?`, etc.).  I need methods to track the current question: `current_question`, to determine the `total_questions`, and to check `has_next_question?`.

Now, I'm designing the game state transition methods. The `start!` method changes the game from "lobby" to "question_open" and sets the current question index to zero, as well as updating the start time and versioning. `finish_question!` closes the current question. `next_question!` moves to the next question, only if the game is in the "question_closed" state.  `end_quiz!` marks the game as "finished". I also need the `join_player!(name:)` method to add players to the game. It handles player creation, and error checking. The `submit_answer!(player:, game_question_id:, game_option_id:)` method needs to handle answer submissions, ensuring the question is open and valid, and it updates the answer if one exists. Both `join_player!` and `submit_answer!` should broadcast the game state.

Finally, I'm structuring payloads for different users:

*   **`moderator_payload`:** This will expose the whole state of the game: versions, status, code, quiz title, player count, total questions, current question index, the question body and options, and whether the question is open or closed, as well as the question index and total. When the question is closed, it includes the number of answers and the correct answers for each option. This will be broadcast.
*   **`player_public_payload`:** This will hold the information available to all players: version, status, and quiz title. If the game is in question states, the body and options will also be included, and, only if the question is closed, the correct answer for each option will be included.
*   **`player_payload(player)`:** This builds upon `player_public_payload` but also includes the player's name and their submitted answer's ID, if they've answered.

I'm making a point to ensure that the `player_public_payload` never exposes the correct answer when the question is open. That should be fine; it's only included when the status is "question_closed".

class Game < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[lobby question_open question_closed finished].freeze
  CODE_ALPHABET = "ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789".chars.freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :players, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :answers, dependent: :destroy

  validates :code, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :status, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }

  def self.generate_unique_code
    loop do
      candidate = Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET.sample }.join
      return candidate unless exists?(code: candidate)
    end
  end

  def self.create_for_quiz!(quiz)
    active_questions = quiz.questions.active.ordered.includes(:options).to_a
    raise ArgumentError, "Quiz has no active questions" if active_questions.empty?

    transaction do
      game = quiz.games.create!(code: generate_unique_code, status: "lobby")
      active_questions.each_with_index do |q, q_idx|
        gq = game.game_questions.create!(
          question_id: q.id,
          body: q.body,
          position: q_idx + 1
        )
        q.options.each_with_index do |opt, o_idx|
          gq.game_options.create!(
            option_id: opt.id,
            body: opt.body,
            correct: opt.correct?,
            position: o_idx + 1
          )
        end
      end
      game
    end
  end

  def lobby?
    status == "lobby"
  end

  def question_open?
    status == "question_open"
  end

  def question_closed?
    status == "question_closed"
  end

  def finished?
    status == "finished"
  end

  def ordered_questions
    game_questions.order(:position, :id)
  end

  def current_question
    ordered_questions.offset(current_question_index).first
  end

  def total_questions
    game_questions.count
  end

  def has_next_question?
    current_question_index < total_questions - 1
  end

  def start!
    changed = false
    with_lock do
      if lobby? && game_questions.exists?
        update!(
          status: "question_open",
          current_question_index: 0,
          started_at: Time.current,
          state_version: state_version + 1,
          phase_version: phase_version + 1
        )
        changed = true
      end
    end
    broadcast_state!(include_players: true) if changed
    changed
  end

  def finish_question!
    changed = false
    with_lock do
      if question_open?
        update!(
          status: "question_closed",
          state_version: state_version + 1,
          phase_version: phase_version + 1
        )
        changed = true
      end
    end
    broadcast_state!(include_players: true) if changed
    changed
  end

  def next_question!
    changed = false
    with_lock do
      if question_closed? && has_next_question?
        update!(
          status: "question_open",
          current_question_index: current_question_index + 1,
          state_version: state_version + 1,
          phase_version: phase_version + 1
        )
        changed = true
      end
    end
    broadcast_state!(include_players: true) if changed
    changed
  end

  def end_quiz!
    changed = false
    with_lock do
      if question_closed? && !has_next_question?
        update!(
          status: "finished",
          finished_at: Time.current,
          state_version: state_version + 1,
          phase_version: phase_version + 1
        )
        changed = true
      end
    end
    broadcast_state!(include_players: true) if changed
    changed
  end

  def join_player!(name:)
    trimmed = name.to_s.strip
    player = nil
    with_lock do
      return [ nil, "The quiz is over" ] if finished?

      player = players.build(name: trimmed)
      unless player.save
        return [ nil, player.errors.full_messages.first || "Your name can't be blank" ]
      end

      update!(state_version: state_version + 1)
    end
    broadcast_state!(include_players: false)
    [ player, nil ]
  end

  def submit_answer!(player:, game_question_id:, game_option_id:)
    result = nil
    with_lock do
      cq = current_question
      unless question_open? && cq && cq.id == game_question_id.to_i
        return { accepted: false }
      end

      option = cq.game_options.find_by(id: game_option_id)
      return { accepted: false } unless option

      answer = answers.find_or_initialize_by(player_id: player.id, game_question_id: cq.id)
      answer.game_option_id = option.id
      answer.save!

      update!(state_version: state_version + 1)
      result = { accepted: true, picked_option_id: option.id }
    end
    broadcast_state!(include_players: false)
    result
  end

  def moderator_payload
    ordered = ordered_questions.includes(:game_options).to_a
    total = ordered.size
    player_count = players.count
    cq = ordered[current_question_index]

    payload = {
      version: state_version,
      phase_version: phase_version,
      status: status,
      code: code,
      quiz_title: quiz.title,
      player_count: player_count,
      total_questions: total,
      current_question_index: current_question_index
    }

    if cq && (question_open? || question_closed?)
      answered_count = answers.where(game_question_id: cq.id).count
      counts_by_option = if question_closed?
        answers.where(game_question_id: cq.id).group(:game_option_id).count
      else
        {}
      end

      payload[:answered_count] = answered_count
      payload[:has_next_question] = current_question_index < total - 1
      payload[:question] = {
        id: cq.id,
        index: current_question_index + 1,
        total: total,
        body: cq.body,
        options: cq.game_options.map do |opt|
          opt_data = {
            id: opt.id,
            body: opt.body
          }
          if question_closed?
            opt_data[:correct] = opt.correct?
            opt_data[:count] = counts_by_option.fetch(opt.id, 0)
          end
          opt_data
        end
      }
    end

    payload
  end

  def player_public_payload
    ordered = ordered_questions.includes(:game_options).to_a
    total = ordered.size
    cq = ordered[current_question_index]

    payload = {
      version: phase_version,
      status: status,
      quiz_title: quiz.title
    }

    if cq && (question_open? || question_closed?)
      payload[:question] = {
        id: cq.id,
        index: current_question_index + 1,
        total: total,
        body: cq.body,
        options: cq.game_options.map do |opt|
          opt_data = {
            id: opt.id,
            body: opt.body
          }
          opt_data[:correct] = opt.correct? if question_closed?
          opt_data
        end
      }
    end

    payload
  end

  def player_payload(player)
    payload = player_public_payload
    payload[:player_name] = player&.name

    if player && payload[:question]
      answer = answers.find_by(player_id: player.id, game_question_id: payload[:question][:id])
      payload[:picked_option_id] = answer&.game_option_id
    else
      payload[:picked_option_id] = nil
    end

    payload
  end

  def broadcast_state!(include_players: true)
    ActionCable.server.broadcast("moderate_game_#{id}", moderator_payload)
    ActionCable.server.broadcast("player_game_#{id}", player_public_payload) if include_players
  end
end

  def subscribed
    game = Game.find_by(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
